Add, increment, double, the register and the rest are written as hand-listed cases in `FirstParts` and `ArithmeticParts` and again as functions in `Specifications.Counted`, looked up by name with " 4-bit" stripped; latencies are two formulas (`ArithmeticParts.LoopLatency` and `Specification.Loop`); the register contract exists twice with different values; and `TaskSuite` defines n+1, 2n and n1+n2 a third time.
We want each contract built from its `Specification` (function, domain, latency, port layout) by one case builder, with the catalogue holding specifications rather than case lists.

Its responsibilities are:
* A case builder that makes a contract's cases from a specification and the values to use
* `FirstParts` and `ArithmeticParts` rewritten as specifications plus case values, with the `Start`/`Done`/`Case` helpers shared
* One latency formula per specification
* One register contract, removing the patch in `HandBuiltParts`
* `TaskSuite`'s function tasks taken from the same specifications
* Port layout computed once, in place of `Part.Ports()`, `ContractTask.Boundary` and `PortBinding.AfterInputs`

Built contracts should equal today's contracts case for case, checked by a test against the current lists before they are deleted, because parts on disk are loaded only if their contract matches the catalogue's.
This should not add held-out cases or domains, because that is the algorithm spec in M4 and this ticket only removes the second copy.

Where: `SNP_Evolution/Evolution/Contracts/Specification.cs`, `FirstParts.cs`, `ArithmeticParts.cs`, `ReferenceParts.cs`, `HandBuiltParts.cs`, `PortBinding.cs`, `SNP_Evolution/Evolution/Tasks/TaskSuite.cs`, `SNP_Evolution/Evolution/Tasks/ContractTask.cs`.

Done when:
- [ ] Every catalogue contract is built from a specification and equals the old list (test kept until the lists are removed)
- [ ] `Specifications` is not looked up by a name string anywhere
- [ ] Golden runs unchanged; every part in `parts/` and `parts-profile/` loads; `dotnet test` green

Read first: RESEARCH.md "Proving contracts" (Specifications)
